summary: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Count forward starting from a given number.
Write numerals 0 to 20 and use one to show how many objects (0 for none).
Count objects one-to-one, know the last number is the total, and next is one more, previous one less.
Name how many in a quick look at up to 5 objects without counting (perceptual subitizing).
Count up to 20 arranged or 10 scattered objects; count out a set of 1 to 20.
Tell whether one group (up to 10) has more, fewer or the same as another.
Compare two written numerals from 1 to 10, recording the comparison in your own way.
Show addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, drawings, sounds, acting out or numbers.
Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
Break numbers up to 10 into pairs in several ways; name quick-look amounts to 10 (subitizing).
For a number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 with it.
Add and subtract within 5 flexibly and efficiently using mental images.
Show numbers 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones, recording with drawings or numbers.
Describe measurable attributes like length or weight, several for one object.
Compare two objects directly by a shared attribute and say which has more or less.
Sort objects into categories, count each category, and order categories by count (up to 10).
Name shapes in the surroundings and describe positions like above, below, beside, next to.
Name shapes correctly whatever their size or orientation.
Tell whether shapes are flat (two-dimensional) or solid (three-dimensional).
Compare flat and solid shapes, describing sides, corners and other attributes informally.
Build shapes from materials like sticks and clay, and draw shapes.
Put simple shapes together to make larger shapes.
Solve all types of addition and subtraction story problems within 20, unknown in any position.
Solve story problems adding three whole numbers with a sum up to 20.
Use properties of addition (order, grouping) informally as strategies.
See subtraction as finding a missing addend.
Relate counting on to adding and subtracting, and use quick-look grouping (subitizing) up to 20.
Add and subtract within 20 with several strategies; flexible and efficient within 10.
Know the equal sign means "same value as" and judge equations true or false.
Count to 120 from any number; read, write and match numerals to sets of objects.
Know the two digits of a two-digit number are tens and ones, including teens and decades.
Compare two-digit numbers by tens and ones, describing the result in words and >, =, <.
Add within 100 (two-digit plus one-digit or a multiple of 10) with models and place value.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number mentally and explain.
Subtract multiples of 10 from 10 to 90 using models and place-value strategies.
Order three objects by length and compare two lengths using a third object.
Measure length by laying same-size units end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Organize and interpret data with up to three categories and answer questions about it.
Tell defining from non-defining shape attributes; build and draw shapes with given attributes.
Put flat or solid shapes together into composite shapes and make new shapes from them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths and count the shares; more shares are smaller.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction story problems within 100.
Add and subtract within 20 flexibly with mental strategies; memorizing all sums is not stated.
Decide if a group of up to 20 is odd or even and write even numbers as doubles.
Use repeated addition to find the total in arrays up to 5 by 5.
Know the digits of a three-digit number are hundreds, tens and ones, with 100 as ten tens.
Count within 1,000 and skip-count by 5s, 10s and 100s.
Read and write numbers to 1,000 in numerals, words and expanded form.
Compare three-digit numbers by place value, describing the result in words and >, =, <.
Add and subtract within 100 flexibly and efficiently with place-value strategies.
Add up to four two-digit numbers using place value and properties.
Add and subtract within 1,000 with models and place value, regrouping when needed.
Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from numbers 100 to 900.
Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work using place value and properties.
Measure length by choosing and using rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks or tapes.
Measure an object in two different units and relate the results to unit size.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Measure how much longer one object is than another in standard units.
Solve length story problems within 100 in the same units, writing an equation.
Show whole numbers, sums and differences within 100 on a number line.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes with a.m. and p.m.
Solve money story problems with bills and coins using $ and cent signs.
Measure lengths to the nearest whole unit and show the data on a line plot.
Draw picture and bar graphs with up to four categories and solve problems from them.
Draw and identify shapes with given attributes: triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, cubes.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths; equal shares can differ in shape.
Interpret a product as the total in a number of equal groups.
Interpret a quotient as a share size or a number of shares.
Solve multiplication and division word problems within 100 with groups, arrays and measures.
Use properties of multiplication (order, grouping, distributive) as strategies.
See division as finding a missing factor.
Build multiply/divide strategies within 100; quick facts only for 0, 1, 2, 5 and 10.
Solve two-step word problems with the four operations using one or two equations; check by estimating.
Find and explain patterns in addition and multiplication tables using properties.
Estimate answers to real-world problems within 1,000 with mental math, benchmarks or rounding.
Add and subtract within 1,000 flexibly and efficiently with place-value strategies.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 from 10 to 90.
Understand unit fractions and fractions as made of unit fractions, like 7/4 as seven fourths.
Place fractions on a number line by splitting 0 to 1 into equal parts and repeating them.
Find simple equivalent fractions, write wholes as fractions, compare same-numerator or same-denominator fractions.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems in minutes.
Measure and estimate liquid volume and mass in g, kg and L; solve one-step problems.
Draw scaled picture and bar graphs and solve one- and two-step problems from them.
Measure lengths to the half and quarter inch and show the data on a line plot.
Understand area as covering a flat shape with unit squares.
Measure area by counting unit squares in metric, standard and improvised units.
Link area to multiplication and addition, including the distributive property and rectilinear shapes.
Solve perimeter problems for polygons, including unknown sides and same-area or same-perimeter rectangles.
Sort quadrilaterals such as rhombuses, rectangles and squares by their attributes.
Split shapes into equal-area parts and name each part as a unit fraction.
Read a multiplication equation as a comparison and write comparisons as equations.
Solve multiplicative comparison word problems and tell them apart from additive ones.
Solve multi-step whole-number word problems, interpret remainders, and check with estimation.
Find factor pairs to 100, relate factors and multiples, and tell prime from composite.
Make number or shape patterns from a rule and notice features the rule does not state.
Multiply and divide within 100 flexibly and efficiently using strategies and properties.
Know a digit is worth ten times what it is worth one place to the right.
Read, write and compare multi-digit numbers in numerals, words and expanded form.
Estimate with multi-digit whole numbers using mental math, benchmarks, compatible numbers or rounding.
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers with strategies or algorithms; standard algorithm not required.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit, and two digits by two digits, explaining with models.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with remainders, explaining with models.
Explain and make equivalent fractions using visual models and a general rule.
Compare fractions with unlike numerators and denominators using benchmarks or common parts.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like and related denominators like 1/2 + 1/4.
Multiply a whole number by a fraction with models, including word problems.
Rewrite tenths as hundredths to add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.
Write fractions with denominator 10 or 100 as decimals and show them on models.
Compare decimals to hundredths by reasoning and benchmarks, using >, =, <.
Know relative sizes of units in one system and convert larger units to smaller in a table.
Solve word problems on distance, time, volume, mass and money, including unit conversions.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real and math problems.
Make line plots of measurements in halves, quarters and eighths and solve problems from them.
Understand angles as two rays from a point, measured in degrees of a circle.
Measure and sketch angles in whole degrees with a protractor.
Add angle measures and find unknown angles in diagrams.
Draw and identify points, lines, segments, rays, angle types, and parallel or perpendicular lines.
Classify flat shapes by parallel or perpendicular lines and angle types; identify right triangles.
Find and draw lines of symmetry.
Use and evaluate expressions with parentheses, brackets or braces.
Write simple expressions from calculations and interpret them without evaluating.
Make two patterns from two rules, relate their terms, and graph them as ordered pairs.
A digit is worth 10 times the place to its right and 1/10 the place to its left.
Explain zero and decimal-point patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10.
Read, write and compare decimals to thousandths, including expanded form.
Estimate with decimals using mental math, benchmarks, compatible numbers or rounding.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers with strategies or algorithms; standard algorithm not required.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit numbers, explaining with models.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths with models and strategies.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators using equivalent fractions.
Solve fraction addition and subtraction word problems and estimate with benchmarks.
See a fraction as equal sharing (division) and solve division problems with fraction answers.
Multiply fractions by whole numbers or fractions, including areas with fractional sides.
Understand multiplication as scaling: predict if a product is bigger or smaller than a factor.
Solve real problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers, and estimate.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions, including word problems.
Convert units within one measurement system and use them in multi-step problems.
Make line plots of measurements in halves, quarters and eighths and solve problems from them.
Understand volume as filling a solid with unit cubes.
Measure volume by counting unit cubes in cubic cm, in, ft and improvised units.
Find rectangular prism volume with V = lwh or Bh and add volumes of joined prisms.
Understand the coordinate plane: axes, origin and ordered pairs.
Graph and interpret points in the first quadrant for real and math problems.
Know attributes of a shape category belong to all its subcategories.
Classify flat shapes in a hierarchy by their properties.

state_code: # - Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (adopted May 2021; current): https://dpi.wi.gov/sites/default/files/imce/standards/New%20pdfs/MathematicsStandards2021.pdf
# - Official crosswalk: "2010 to 2021 Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics Comparison, K-8" (WI adopted CCSS in 2010, so 2010 codes = CCSS):
# - M.<grade>.<domain>.<cluster letter>.<number>, e.g. M.K.CC.B.6, M.1.MD.B.3, M.4.OA.D.6. Same shape as full CCSS codes plus an "M." prefix.
# - Where WI inserted a standard, later numbers in that cluster shift and the PDF prints the old code, e.g. M.K.CC.B.6 [WI.2010.K.CC.B.5].
#   Shifted codes: M.K.CC.B.6/C.7/C.8 = CCSS K.CC.B.5/C.6/C.7; M.3.OA.B.4/B.5/C.6/D.7/D.8 = CCSS 3.OA.B.5/B.6/C.7/D.8/D.9
#   (the PDF prints the old grade 3 codes with cluster B throughout, e.g. "3.OA.B.8"; the comparison document shows 3.OA.5-3.OA.9).
#   Do not match WI codes to CCSS by code string in K.CC and 3.OA.
# - Lettered sub-parts (a, b, ...) are not separately coded; folded into their standard.
# CCSS K-5 STANDARDS DROPPED (2010 standard with no 2021 counterpart in the official comparison):
#   1.OA.D.8 = find the unknown in an addition/subtraction equation; 3.OA.A.4 = find the unknown in a multiplication/division equation.
# - New: perceptual subitizing up to 5 (M.K.CC.B.5); conceptual subitizing added inside M.K.OA.A.3 (b) and M.1.OA.C.5 (b).
# - Moved later: full multiplication/division fluency within 100 is grade 4 (M.4.OA.D.6, = CCSS 3.OA.C.7); grade 3 (M.3.OA.C.6)
#   expects strategies plus quick facts only for multiples of 0, 1, 2, 5 and 10. 2.OA.B.2 no longer says to know sums from memory.
# - Moved earlier: grade 4 adds fractions with related denominators like 1/2 + 1/4 (M.4.NF.B.3, part of CCSS 5.NF.A.1).
# - Rounding standards (3.NBT.A.1, 4.NBT.A.3, 5.NBT.A.4) become estimation standards (mental math, benchmarks, compatible numbers, rounding).
# - "Fluently" is replaced by "flexibly and efficiently" throughout; 4.NBT.B.4 and 5.NBT.B.5 drop the standard algorithm requirement.
# - Many standards add "describe the comparison in words and symbols" and visual-model examples (tape diagrams, number lines); treated as same.
# - M.K.CC.B.4 adds "previous number is one smaller": marked edited (small).
# - M.4.NF.B.3 maps to 4.NF.B.3 and 5.NF.A.1 (related denominators only); kind edited.
# - M.3.OA.D.7 (two-step problems, one or two equations, rounding no longer named) kept as same with 3.OA.D.8.
# - 1.G.A.3 drops the word "quarters"; 2.MD.B.5 uses number lines instead of ruler drawings: same.
# - kind is judged on content: same = CCSS content with only rewording or small example changes.
